---
title: "01_contrast_tiers"
output: html_document
---

Purpose: decide, per species and per model part, which levels of the stage contrast the data can
support, and write the species table and the cluster job table for the stage 1 contrast models.
Definitions and rules are in `README.md`; constants are in `contrast_data_functions.R`.

In short:

- **event**: a run of survey dates at one site with no gap over 5 days; runs longer than 14 days
  are split at their longest gap
- **co-sampled unit** (event, site-year, population): >= 5 swabs of each stage (and, for load,
  >= 1 positive swab of each stage)
- **inclusion**: >= 20 swabs of each stage and >= 1 co-sampled population
- **contrast levels**, separately for prevalence (hu) and load (mu): the contrast varies at a
  level with >= 3 co-sampled sites / 5 site-years / 10 events, and only if it also varies at the
  level above; none at all if < 25% of swabs are in co-sampled sites (between-population).
  **tier** = the result: A (site, site-year, event), B (site, site-year), C (site), D (mean
  contrast only); load "none" when a stage has no positives
- **flag**: time-segregated (>= 3 co-sampled site-years, fewer than half as many co-sampled
  events); a caveat only
- **nuisance structure** (added after the first cluster fits): R2 drop a site-year / event
  intercept level that barely splits its parent; R3 sigma varies by population only with >= 3
  populations with >= 10 positives

Run order: `size_bd_unified/01_model_data.Rmd` (model data), then this script.

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| output: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show setup code"

librarian::shelf(tidyverse, here)

intermediates_dir = here("size_bd_contrast", "intermediates")
dir.create(intermediates_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Data file created by size_bd_unified/01_model_data.Rmd
load(here("size_bd_unified", "intermediates", "bd_model_env_unified_2026-11-12.RData"))

source(here("size_bd_contrast", "contrast_data_functions.R"))

```

# Data
```{r}
# stage_c, pop_year and pop_year_event (survey-run events) added; see contrast_data_functions.R
contrast_data = add_contrast_groups(brms_data)

# swabs and positives per stage, per species
stage_counts = contrast_data %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, life_stage_simple) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), n_pos = sum(.data[[response_col]] > 0), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = life_stage_simple, values_from = c(n, n_pos), values_fill = 0)

```

# Event definition screen
```{r}
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-width: 12

# the evidence behind the event definition and swab threshold used for the tiers. co-sampled
# units per species under several unit definitions, finest to coarsest, at two swab thresholds:
#   population:date        one site visit
#   survey run             the event used: dates with no gap > 5 days, runs > 14 days split at
#                          their longest gap (pop_year_event, contrast_data_functions.R)
#   population:year:2wk / 3wk / 4wk
#                          14 / 21 / 28-day bins of day of year (bins cut at the new year; 2wk
#                          was the round 1-2 event)
#   population:year:month  calendar month
#   population:year        site-year (the tier B level; also m11g's population:year)
#   population             both stages ever found at the site (inclusion; population-level contrast)
# thresholds: >= 2 swabs of each stage is lenient (a very noisy unit-level contrast); >= 5 shows
# how much of the information is solid.
#
# what this decided:
#   - 2026-11-24: threshold = 5 swabs of each stage (min_swabs_unit). at >= 2, several species
#     reach tier A only through events with 2-4 swabs per stage (e.g. l. sphenocephalus: 24
#     events at >= 2, 1 at >= 5), whose event-level contrasts would barely be informed. counts
#     barely change between single dates and 2-, 3- or 4-week bins (merging nearby visits lowers
#     the count, pooling their swabs lets more units reach the threshold; the two roughly cancel).
#   - 2026-11-25: event = survey run instead of 2-week bins (round 3). bins cut 138 visit runs
#     at an arbitrary calendar edge, leaving two near-duplicate events with fewer swabs each.
#     gaps between survey dates peak at 1 day (consecutive-day designs) and again at 7 and 14
#     (weekly / fortnightly programs), so a 5-day gap groups consecutive days without chaining
#     weekly revisits (a 7-day gap chained a. canorus 2021 into a 76-day "event"). intensive
#     resurvey periods (visits every 2-5 days for up to 24 days) are split at 14 days, the bins'
#     resolution. a 3-day gap would drop c. panamansis below the event threshold (10 -> 9).
#     no tier changes; see the run summary below.
screen_data = contrast_data %>%
  mutate(pop_date = paste(population, date, sep = "_"),
         pop_year_2wk = paste(population, year, (yday(date) - 1) %/% 14, sep = "_"),
         pop_year_3wk = paste(population, year, (yday(date) - 1) %/% 21, sep = "_"),
         pop_year_4wk = paste(population, year, (yday(date) - 1) %/% 28, sep = "_"),
         pop_year_month = paste(population, year, month(date), sep = "_"))

unit_defs = c(`population:date` = "pop_date",
              `survey run` = "pop_year_event",
              `population:year:2wk` = "pop_year_2wk",
              `population:year:3wk` = "pop_year_3wk",
              `population:year:4wk` = "pop_year_4wk",
              `population:year:month` = "pop_year_month",
              `population:year` = "pop_year",
              population = "population")

# one count per definition x threshold, using the same function as the tiers
event_screen = expand_grid(unit_def = names(unit_defs), min_swabs = c(2, 5)) %>%
  pmap_dfr(function(unit_def, min_swabs) {
    count_co_units(screen_data, unit_defs[[unit_def]], min_swabs = min_swabs) %>%
      mutate(unit_def = unit_def, min_swabs = min_swabs, .after = taxon_capture)
  }) %>%
  mutate(unit_def = factor(unit_def, levels = names(unit_defs)))

# wide: co-sampled units (prevalence / load) per definition and threshold, one row per species
event_screen %>%
  mutate(value = paste0(n_co, " / ", n_co_load),
         col = paste0(unit_def, " (>=", min_swabs, ")")) %>%
  select(taxon_capture, col, value) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = value) %>%
  arrange(taxon_capture)

ggplot(event_screen, aes(x = n_co + 1, y = fct_rev(taxon_capture), color = unit_def)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = min_co_events_slope + 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ min_swabs, labeller = labeller(min_swabs = function(x) paste0(">= ", x, " swabs of each stage"))) +
  labs(x = "co-sampled units + 1 (log scale)", y = NULL, color = "unit",
       subtitle = paste0("prevalence definition; dashed = event-level contrast threshold (", min_co_events_slope, " units)")) +
  theme_minimal()

# survey-run events: how long they are, and how they compare to the 2-week bins.
# span = first to last survey date, inclusive (1 = a single day)
event_spans = contrast_data %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, pop_year_event) %>%
  summarise(span = as.numeric(max(date) - min(date)) + 1, n_dates = n_distinct(date),
            n_bins = n_distinct((yday(date) - 1) %/% 14), .groups = "drop")

event_spans %>%
  count(span = cut(span, c(0, 1, 3, 5, 7, 10, 14), include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))

# runs that the 2-week bins would have split (a bin edge falls inside the run)
event_spans %>%
  summarise(events = n(), max_span = max(span), split_by_bins = sum(n_bins > 1))

# the longest events (> 10 days), with swabs per survey date (adults / subadults): these are
# intensive resurvey periods; most hold a single stage
contrast_data %>%
  semi_join(event_spans %>% filter(span > 10), by = c("taxon_capture", "pop_year_event")) %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, pop_year_event, date) %>%
  summarise(n_ad = sum(life_stage_simple == "adult"), n_sub = sum(life_stage_simple == "subadult"),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, pop_year_event) %>%
  summarise(span = as.numeric(max(date) - min(date)) + 1,
            dates = paste0(format(date, "%m-%d"), " (", n_ad, "/", n_sub, ")", collapse = ", "),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(span))

```

# Co-sampled units
```{r}
# one count per unit type; columns renamed by level so they can sit side by side.
# events -> informs the event-level contrast (tier A); site-years -> tier B; populations ->
# inclusion and the population-level contrast
co_counts = list(event = "pop_year_event", popyear = "pop_year", pop = "population") %>%
  imap(function(unit, level) {
    count_co_units(contrast_data, unit) %>%
      rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_", level), -taxon_capture)
  }) %>%
  reduce(left_join, by = "taxon_capture")

co_counts

```

# Inclusion, tiers and flag
```{r}
# contrast levels rule (contrast_tier, contrast_data_functions.R; README "Contrast levels"):
# prevalence uses the prevalence co-sampled counts, load the load counts. the between-population
# share (pct_swabs_in_co_pop) is one species-level number used for both parts.
# time-segregated flag: stages often meet in the same site-year but rarely in the same survey
# event (adults and subadults swabbed at different times of year), so part of the contrast
# compares different times of year. a caveat only; it does not change the model.
species_table = stage_counts %>%
  left_join(co_counts, by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  # nuisance structure (README "Nuisance structure"): which levels each part can separate (R2:
  # hu_has_pop_year, ...) and sigma_by_population (R3). needed first: a contrast slope cannot
  # sit on a dropped level
  left_join(level_structure(contrast_data), by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  mutate(
    include = n_adult >= min_n_stage & n_subadult >= min_n_stage & n_co_pop >= min_co_pops,
    exclude_reason = case_when(
      n_adult < min_n_stage | n_subadult < min_n_stage ~ paste0("< ", min_n_stage, " swabs of a stage"),
      n_co_pop < min_co_pops ~ "no co-sampled population",
      .default = NA_character_),
    between_population = pct_swabs_in_co_pop < min_pct_swabs_co_pop,
    tier_hu = contrast_tier(n_co_pop, n_co_popyear, n_co_event, pct_swabs_in_co_pop,
                            hu_has_pop_year, hu_has_event),
    # load part: no stage term if a stage has no positive swabs (contrast not estimable)
    tier_mu = contrast_tier(n_co_load_pop, n_co_load_popyear, n_co_load_event, pct_swabs_in_co_pop,
                            mu_has_pop_year, mu_has_event,
                            none = n_pos_adult == 0 | n_pos_subadult == 0),
    d_reason_hu = d_reason(tier_hu, n_co_pop, pct_swabs_in_co_pop),
    d_reason_mu = d_reason(tier_mu, n_co_load_pop, pct_swabs_in_co_pop),
    flag_time_segregated = n_co_popyear >= time_seg_min_popyears &
      n_co_event < n_co_popyear * time_seg_max_event_ratio) %>%
  mutate(across(c(tier_hu, tier_mu, d_reason_hu, d_reason_mu), ~ if_else(include, .x, NA_character_))) %>%
  arrange(desc(include), tier_hu, tier_mu, taxon_capture)

# excluded species and why
species_table %>%
  filter(!include) %>%
  select(taxon_capture, n_adult, n_subadult, n_co_pop, exclude_reason)

# included species: tiers (with the reason for D), the counts behind them, and the flag
species_table %>%
  filter(include) %>%
  select(taxon_capture, tier_hu, d_reason_hu, tier_mu, d_reason_mu,
         n_co_pop, n_co_popyear, n_co_event, n_co_load_pop, n_co_load_popyear, n_co_load_event,
         pct_swabs_in_co_pop, flag_time_segregated)

# tier cross-tab (prevalence x load)
species_table %>%
  filter(include) %>%
  count(tier_hu, tier_mu)

# nuisance structure: species with a dropped intercept level (R2) or a constant sigma (R3)
species_table %>%
  filter(include) %>%
  select(taxon_capture, hu_py_per_pop, hu_ev_per_py, mu_py_per_pop, mu_ev_per_py,
         hu_has_pop_year, hu_has_event, mu_has_pop_year, mu_has_event,
         n_pops_pos_sigma, sigma_by_population) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  filter(!(hu_has_pop_year & hu_has_event & mu_has_pop_year & mu_has_event) | !sigma_by_population)

```

# Cluster jobs
```{r}
# one row per model fit. main fits use each species' tiers; sensitivity fits override them (the
# level and sigma structure columns come from the species either way).
# anaxyrus_canorus: tier C by the rule (load: D), but a focal species with 13 co-sampled
# events at >= 2 swabs, so also fit with the tier A structure for both parts.
sensitivity_jobs = tribble(
  ~taxon_capture,      ~variant,     ~tier_hu, ~tier_mu,
  "anaxyrus_canorus",  "sens_tierA", "A",      "A")

# columns the model builders read (contrast_model_functions.R): tiers, levels present per part,
# sigma structure
structure_cols = c("hu_has_pop_year", "hu_has_event", "mu_has_pop_year", "mu_has_event",
                   "sigma_by_population")

contrast_jobs = species_table %>%
  filter(include) %>%
  transmute(taxon_capture, variant = "main", tier_hu, tier_mu) %>%
  bind_rows(sensitivity_jobs) %>%
  left_join(species_table %>% select(taxon_capture, all_of(structure_cols), n_adult, n_subadult,
                                     d_reason_hu, d_reason_mu, flag_time_segregated),
            by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  mutate(n = n_adult + n_subadult,
         # the reason for D belongs to the species' own tier: clear it where a sensitivity fit
         # overrides that tier
         d_reason_hu = if_else(tier_hu == "D", d_reason_hu, NA_character_),
         d_reason_mu = if_else(tier_mu == "D", d_reason_mu, NA_character_)) %>%
  arrange(taxon_capture, variant) %>%
  # 0-based, as SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID
  mutate(array_index = row_number() - 1)

contrast_jobs

```

# Export
```{r}
write_csv(event_screen, file.path(intermediates_dir, "01_contrast_event_screen.csv"))
write_csv(species_table, file.path(intermediates_dir, "01_contrast_species.csv"))
write_csv(contrast_jobs, file.path(intermediates_dir, "01_contrast_jobs.csv"))
```
